newsitem.title: PORTUGAL: Portugal opposition to abstain in budget vote.
newsitem.headline: Portugal opposition to abstain in budget vote.

text.p: Portugal's largest opposition party, the Social Democrats, said on Monday that it would abstain in this week's parliamentary vote on the minority Socialist government's budget.

The budget, which is vital to Portugal's hopes of qualifying for the European Union's single currency, was already certain to pass the legislature after the small, right-wing Popular Party said that it would not oppose it.

Social Democrat leader Marcelo Rebelo de Sousa told journalists after meeting Prime Minister Antonio Guterres that his party had opted to abstain in the "interests of the Portuguese and the single currency."

The Social Democrats, like the government, are strong supporters of Europe and want Portugal to form part of the vanguard of European Union countries that moves to Economic and Monetary Union (EMU) in 1999.
Making the grade for EMU involves meeting tough economic tests in 1997, including reducing the budget deficit and inflation.
"The most important thing at the moment is stability -- political, economic and monetary," Rebelo de Sousa said.
The government is four seats short of an absolute majority in the 230-seat parliament where the budget will be put to the vote on Wednesday or Thursday.
